title: Deploy collector: pull recent release events and post deploy summary blocks to incident threads
author: Jacob Stein
commits: deploy_collector: implement v1 collector backed by Release Events API
release events client: add retry/backoff + region/service normalization
slack formatting: add deploy summary block renderer + truncation rules
tests: fixtures + unit tests for mapping + time window selection
body:
Context
This PR adds the initial Deploy Collector implementation (v1) for the incident context bundle. The collector pulls recent deploy/release events, maps them to the impacted service + region(s), and posts a compact summary block into the incident Slack thread.

Motivation
During early incident triage we repeatedly spend the first few minutes answering “what changed?” (especially in multi-region). Having the bot attach the last few deploys per service/region (with links) has been one of the highest-signal requests from on-call (see ENG-2842; motivating example in SUP-4921).

What’s included
- DeployCollector (plugin) implementation using the collector framework added in #123.
- Release events client:
  - Fetches from Release Events API (release pipeline event stream) by time window + optional service filter.
  - Normalizes service names (release pipeline names -> bot service keys) using service_registry mapping.
  - Normalizes region tags (e.g., us-east-1, use1, iad -> us-east-1).
  - Retries on 5xx with bounded backoff; hard timeout enforced by framework.
- Selection logic:
  - Default window: last 60 minutes OR last 2 deploys (whichever yields fewer items), per service/region.
  - Includes manual rollbacks/hotfix deploy events and marks them as rollback when the event has rollback_of populated.
  - Canary awareness: if rollout metadata exists, show canary %; otherwise omit (don’t guess).
- Slack output:
  - Posts one “Recent deploys” section per impacted service, grouped by region.
  - Compact formatting designed for the first 2–3 minutes of triage; truncates after 6 entries per service and adds “+N more” with a link to the release dashboard.
  - Always includes consistent timestamps (UTC + relative time) to avoid confusion across regions.

Example output (sanitized)
Recent deploys (last 60m)
- gateway-api (us-east-1)
  - 12:41Z (18m ago) v2025.02.06.3 • canary 10% • PR #18421 • pipeline run 983112
  - 12:18Z (41m ago) v2025.02.06.2 • PR #18407 • pipeline run 983044
- gateway-api (eu-west-1)
  - 12:36Z (23m ago) v2025.02.06.3 • canary 10% • PR #18421 • pipeline run 983097

Notes / guardrails
- The collector does not fetch commit messages or any payload fields that could contain customer data.
- If the Release Events API is unavailable/slow, the collector fails open and posts: “Deploy context unavailable (release events timed out)”, with a request id for debugging.
- Region/service mapping is intentionally conservative: unknown service names are skipped (with a debug log) rather than misattributed.

Configuration
- collector_defaults.yaml
  - deploy_collector.enabled: true (behind the global incident bot enable flag)
  - deploy_collector.max_items_per_service: 6
  - deploy_collector.window_minutes: 60
  - deploy_collector.max_deploys_per_region: 2

Testing
- Unit tests cover:
  - event->(service, region) mapping
  - window vs “last N deploys” selection logic
  - rollback labeling behavior
  - slack rendering (stable snapshot tests)
- Fixture-based integration tests validate parsing against representative payloads from use1/euw1.

Rollout
- This is safe to enable in beta channels once the release events source is stable in all regions.
- Follow-up work:
  - Add explicit canary phase labels once schema v2 lands (ENG-2846).
  - Add “suspected change overlap” heuristic after we have deploy + config collectors posting reliably.

Review notes
- Sean: requested grouping by region and a strict cap to avoid thread spam; implemented max_items_per_service + truncation.
- Connor: requested use of service_registry mapping rather than parsing pipeline names; implemented and added missing entries for gateway-api + router.
- Devon: requested that pipeline run links always be present even when PR link is missing; implemented fallback.

Screenshots/links
- Release dashboard: https://console.redwoodinference.com/internal/releases
- Related: ENG-2842, ENG-2846

Changelog
- Adds DeployCollector v1 for incident context bundles; no customer-facing changes.
conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Formatting looks good, but please cap entries more aggressively. Incidents can be noisy and threads get long fast. Also, group by region explicitly; right now it reads like one global timeline.

Jacob Stein (author): Updated renderer to group by region and added max_items_per_service=6 with truncation (+N more) and a release dashboard link. Also tightened default selection to last 60m OR last 2 deploys per region (whichever yields fewer).

Connor O'Brien (review): Please don’t rely on parsing pipeline names for service; we have edge cases (manual rollbacks, hotfix pipelines). Use the service registry mapping and treat unknowns as unknown (skip) rather than guessing.

Jacob Stein (author): Switched to service_registry mapping + added region_aliases normalization. Unknown services are now skipped with a warning log + metric (deploy_collector_unknown_service_total). Added fixtures for a manual rollback event.

Devon Price (review): For events without a PR link, can we still include pipeline run link? That’s often the fastest way to see what happened. Also watch out for time formats (responders are in multiple timezones).
Jacob Stein (author): Added pipeline-run link as the primary link and PR link as optional secondary. Timestamps are now UTC with relative time, e.g., “12:41Z (18m ago)”.
Rafael Mendes (review): Any concerns with load during large incidents? If multiple incidents request deploy context simultaneously, we should avoid hammering release events.

Jacob Stein (author): Collector framework cache (from #123) is keyed by (incident_id, window_start, window_end). DeployCollector requests are bounded and will hit cache for repeated calls. Also kept default window small and capped items.
Sean Gallagher (review): Looks ready. Please add a short doc page with example output and where the data comes from so responders know what they’re looking at.
Jacob Stein (author): Added docs/collectors/deploy_collector.md with source + example output and troubleshooting tips.
Connor O'Brien (review): Approved after mapping changes.
